A hemangioma is a vascular tumor. The imaging describes a lesion of mostly fat density with some soft-tissue components, not primarily vascular, making hemangioma an unlikely diagnosis.

The clinical record describes a large retroperitoneal mass in the location of the right adrenal gland, predominantly fatty with soft-tissue components, consistent with the definition of an adrenal myelolipoma.

A hibernoma is a benign tumor of brown fat. While it is a fatty tumor, the description of the mass as 'mostly fat density' with 'internal areas of soft-tissue density' and the context of adrenal origin and hematopoietic elements (implied by myelolipoma) do not specifically point to brown fat.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Different tumor type (brown fat vs mature fat/hematopoietic).
